bullets.title: S&P 500 down 2% w/w as Mag 7 leads losses; NDX-SPX vol spread widest in two decades
bullets.body: The S&P 500 fell 1.95-2% on the week with the Nasdaq off 4.60%, driven by megacap tech underperformance. NDX realized ~18 vol points higher than SPX, the widest spread in two decades. The Mag 7 collectively shed over $1T in market cap over the week (NVDA -8.6%, AAPL -6%, GOOGL -8.3%) and are now collectively below 50-day MAs; only three remain above 200-day averages. Meanwhile, the Dow gained +0.60% and Russell 2000 rose +1.02%, with S&P 400/600 outperforming, reflecting meaningful rotation into small/mid-caps, cyclicals, and value.

bullets.title: AI/Semi momentum unwind driven by levered ETF cascade, not fundamentals
bullets.body: The week's tech selloff was amplified by a record negative short-gamma regime ($16bn/1% move), levered ETF rebalancing estimated at $42bn of equity supply Tuesday, and HF net selling at a ~3.4 z-score event for AI Tech Beneficiaries. Korea KOSPI dropped ~10% on regulatory warnings around leveraged single-stock chip ETFs, magnifying the US move. Semis (SOX) fell 5.3% on the week yet ended the prior weeks up big—the unwind was characterized as positioning-driven, not a fundamental AI demand shift.

bullets.title: Micron blowout Q3: 16 strategic customer agreements, $100B+ RPO, supply tight beyond 2027
bullets.body: MU reported F3Q26 revenue $41.46B (+15% vs consensus $35.9B), non-GAAP EPS $25.11 vs $20.86 consensus, and 84.9% gross margin (+320bps). F4Q guidance was $50B revenue and $31 EPS, both ~15-20% above consensus, with ~86% gross margins. MU signed 16 multi-year take-or-pay Strategic Customer Agreements representing ~20% of DRAM and ~33% of NAND volume, with cumulative minimum RPO of ~$100B and floor pricing described as "well above prior cycle peak" GMs. Management sees no line of sight to demand-supply balance; supply improvement expected only gradually in 2028. MU plans to return 100% of excess cash to shareholders starting December 2026.

bullets.title: AAPL and MSFT raising hardware prices 15-25% on memory cost inflation; demand destruction risk elevated
bullets.body: Apple announced price increases of 15-25% on MacBooks and iPads citing data center-driven memory/NAND cost inflation; iPhones were not included but September iPhone 18 increases are expected. Microsoft raised Xbox prices for the third time in 13 months ($100-$150 increase Aug 1), with memory/storage costs up 2.5x and expected to double by fall 2027. Analysts warn Apple's price elasticity may exceed 1.0, meaning demand destruction is likely. These developments drove AAPL shares -6% on the week and are being flagged as a new AI-driven inflation vector for consumer electronics.

bullets.title: Fed likely to hike: multiple banks forecast 50-75bp of tightening; core PCE sticky
bullets.body: BofA forecasts 75bp of Fed rate hikes in 2026 (three hikes), Deutsche Bank 50bp; markets are pricing ~33-40bp by year-end. June FOMC showed nine members anticipating hikes and six looking for two or more. 22V Research has a baseline of 2-3 credibility-oriented hikes beginning late 2026 or early 2027 if core PCE stays above ~0.21%/month. May core PCE printed 0.32% (below some hawkish expectations at 0.38%), but core services ex-housing reaccelerated sharply. The Morgan Stanley view is that Fed stays on hold through 2026 if monthly prints stay ≤0.20%.

bullets.title: Fed Chair Warsh reduces forward guidance, raising rate vol; dollar strengthening
bullets.body: The new Fed chair's approach of minimal forward guidance and meeting-by-meeting decisions is driving higher interest rate volatility. Dollar has rallied ~2.7% month-to-date against major currencies, with gold off 25% from peak as the debasement trade unwinds. Warsh's hawkish debut has reinforced price stability focus: 10-year breakevens dropped ~30bp to ~2.2% since mid-May. JPMorgan recommends SOFR curve flatteners; 10Y yields trading 27bp below model fair value.

bullets.title: Oil collapses ~8-9% on Strait of Hormuz reopening; Brent below pre-conflict levels
bullets.body: WTI fell to $69-72 range after falling 9+ consecutive sessions, with Saudi Arabia resuming crude loadings at Ras Tanura and Persian Gulf exports recovering to ~75% of pre-war levels. Brent fell below pre-conflict levels and JPMorgan revised forecasts down to $86 3Q26, $80 4Q26, and $64 average 2027. The oil decline is broadly disinflationary and supportive of rate-sensitive/consumer cyclical equities, while pressuring energy names. JPMorgan notes the US-Iran MOU removes the geopolitical oil premium and opens the way for Iranian barrels returning through formal channels.

bullets.title: Russell rebalance largest in history at $244bn notional; Communication Services +$11.7bn inflows
bullets.body: The 2026 Russell reconstitution effective June 26 was the largest ever at ~$244bn notional (2021 record was $151bn). NVDA's Russell 1000 Growth upweight surged to $4.23bn from $1.96bn. Mega-caps AAPL, AMZN, MSFT shifted from Growth to Value and were the largest net-sell names. Communication Services expected to receive $11.7bn in passive inflows; Consumer Discretionary to see $9.5bn in outflows. CRWV added to Russell 1000 on voting rights. Semiconductor stocks' extreme positioning heading into rebalance contributed to Tuesday's volatility cascade.

bullets.title: Citi downgrades Tech/Semis to Market Weight; Goldman sees 10-year record net selling in Info Tech
bullets.body: Citi US Equity Strategy cut Information Technology, Semiconductors, and Hardware all from Overweight to Market Weight; upgraded Software to Market Weight from Underweight. Goldman Sachs Prime Services reported the week of June 19-25 saw the largest % net selling of Info Tech and Comm Services combined in over 10 years. Overall global equities saw the largest % net selling in 3 months (-2.9 SDs 1-year). Hedge fund gross leverage fell to 1-year lows. Systematic selling risk: a -2% one-day SPX move would generate ~$30bn of additional supply from macro strategies.

bullets.title: JPMorgan raises S&P 500 YE target to 7,800; consensus PT upgrades from Barclays, Stifel, Tom Lee
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised its S&P 500 year-end price target to 7,800 from 7,600 on strong AI earnings revisions and capex validation; 2026 EPS forecast raised to $350 (+29% y/y), 2027 EPS at $390 (+15%). Barclays and Stifel also raised YE targets to 7,800. Tom Lee raised to 8,000. Piper Sandler base case is 7,500 with upside to 8,200-8,400 if breadth confirms. JPM maintains Tactically Bullish and overweights Tech, AI Upstream (Utilities/Industrials), Defense, Banks, Healthcare; expects AI capex supercycle to continue as the primary growth driver.

bullets.title: All 32 large banks pass Fed stress test; dividend hikes and buybacks follow
bullets.body: The 2026 DFAST results showed the smallest CET1 drawdown in 7 years at 1.6% in the Severely Adverse Scenario. All 32 large banks passed with capital above minimums. JPM, MS, WFC, BNY, STT, PNC raised dividends and repurchase authorizations. WFC raised quarterly dividend ~11% to $0.50; USB raised 3.8% to $0.54. Regional banks outperformed on the week: FITB +7.3%, PNC +5.6%, HBAN +5.6%. Banking sector stress tests are strongest in seven years, and higher-for-longer rates are improving NIM with loan yields resetting while deposit costs remain relatively flat.

bullets.title: Mag 7 / AI Tech rotation to cyclicals, value, and SMID intensifying; leadership broadening
bullets.body: Multiple strategists flagged a "mega rotation" from mega-cap AI to cyclicals, value, and small-caps. Russell 2000 up 21% YTD vs S&P 500 +7.4%; the 3-day Russell outperformance vs NDX was the largest since 2024. Healthcare (+6%), Staples (+3%), Utilities (+4.5%), and REITs (+4%) were the best performing sectors week-on-week as defensive rotation occurred. Rate-sensitive names (Housing, Retail, Travel) benefited from the oil decline and lower 10-year yields. Piper Sandler and multiple others note SPX 40-week new highs indicator remains in buy territory with pullbacks corrective not trend-changing.

bullets.title: Consumer spending resilient despite sentiment collapse; real spending +2.1% y/y in May
bullets.body: PSC's daily consumer confidence survey bottomed well above prior crisis lows and is trending higher, contrasting with the University of Michigan survey (below GFC and COVID troughs). Real consumer spending rose 2.1% y/y in May despite UMich sentiment at multi-decade lows. Visa spending momentum index improving; OpenTable dining at 99.7th YoY percentile; Fiserv dollar volume +7.16% YoY. KeyBanc credit card data showed a +6.5% acceleration in retail spending the week of June 21. The divergence between sentiment and actual spending is consistent with the PSC view that the Michigan index is sending a misleading signal.

bullets.title: OpenAI IPO delays to 2027; government restricts frontier model releases, boosting Chinese AI alternatives
bullets.body: OpenAI is leaning toward delaying its IPO to 2027, unable to achieve a $1T valuation target, and chastened by SPCX's post-IPO performance. The Trump administration asked OpenAI to stagger GPT-5.6 release and ordered Anthropic to restrict foreign access to advanced models. These regulatory actions are accelerating open-source and Chinese model adoption: Z.ai GLM-5.2 is now approaching frontier benchmarks at ~1/6 the cost. Goldman Sachs sees this as the AI race shifting from frontier labs toward model orchestration and open-source, lowering costs but accelerating token deflation.

bullets.title: Levered ETF structural risk elevated; $200bn AUM and $400bn net exposure, gamma at historical highs
bullets.body: Levered ETF AUM hovered around $200bn with $400bn in net exposure; trading volumes 50% above H1 2025 pace. MS estimates levered ETF short gamma at -$16bn/1% move at historical highs, with ¾ of exposure benchmarked to Semis, NDX, or Tech single-names. A -2% one-day SPX selloff would create ~$30bn of additional supply over the following week. On Tuesday, levered ETF rebalancing generated an estimated $42bn of equity supply ($18.5bn in Semis ETFs, $9.5bn in NDX ETFs). Korea KOSPI saw $6bn+ of selling attributed to single-stock leveraged ETF margin calls.

bullets.title: Month/quarter-end rebalancing: ~$26-165bn US equity selling estimated
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs estimated $30bn of US equity selling at 89th percentile into quarter-end. JPMorgan estimated ~$165bn of equity selling/bond buying for pension rebalancing. Pension funds are at 110% funding (highest since 2001), setting the stage for mechanical derisking. Retail actively bought the dip with an estimated $43bn of demand Monday-Thursday (100th percentile), split between single stocks and ETFs, partially offsetting systematic and HF selling. Pensions/asset allocators estimated to bring only ~$3bn of US equity demand into month-end.

bullets.title: AI capex supercycle intact: $800bn in 2026, $1.1tn in 2027; power/grid emerging as bottleneck
bullets.body: Five hyperscalers are on track to spend ~$730B in capex in 2026 (+77% y/y), doubling cumulative ChatGPT-era spend. JPMorgan forecasts $5.5tn AI capex through 2030. Morgan Stanley sees $800bn in 2026 and $1.1tn in 2027 as one of the largest infrastructure buildouts in history. Power availability, grid capacity, labor, permitting, and water are the key limiting factors. The data center boom is broadening from Virginia to Texas. J.P. Morgan's global capex nowcaster is tracking 10.2% annualized growth in Q2 2026.

bullets.title: Google loses key AI researchers; Mag 7 sentiment deteriorates on talent exodus, capex ROI concerns
bullets.body: Google DeepMind lost Nobel laureate John Jumper (AlphaFold) to Anthropic and Noam Shazeer (Attention Is All You Need, Gemini co-lead) to OpenAI, alongside two additional senior researchers. GOOGL fell 5-8.3% on the week. The departures fuel investor concerns Google has ceded AI momentum to Anthropic/OpenAI, especially in coding applications. Separately, hyperscaler FCF concerns are mounting: the narrative that AI capex represents a value transfer from hyperscalers to memory/compute suppliers (e.g., AAPL and MSFT raising prices on memory costs) is pressuring Mag 7 multiples.

bullets.title: Samsung announces $648B, 10-year AI/chip capex plan; SK Hynix files $29.4B US ADR
bullets.body: Samsung is planning a ₩1,000 trillion (~$648B) investment over 10 years spanning chips, AI data centers, batteries, and displays—viewed as broadly positive for semiconductor equipment makers. SK Hynix filed for a $29.4B Nasdaq ADR listing (targeting July 10 trading), which would be the second largest IPO ever, aimed at narrowing its valuation gap with Micron and funding HBM capacity. SK Hynix also announced it controls ~61% of the HBM market vs Micron's 21% and Samsung's 17%.

bullets.title: May trade deficit widens sharply; 2Q GDP tracking cut to ~2.1-2.25%
bullets.body: May trade deficit widened to -$105.7bn as real exports dropped 6.6% m/m (broad-based with softer oil volumes) while imports firmed. JPMorgan trimmed its 2Q GDP forecast from 3.0% to 2.25%; Morgan Stanley cut to 2.1-2.4% from 2.5%. Domestic demand remains more resilient at ~2.4%. U Michigan consumer sentiment rose 4.7pts in June to 49.5 on energy relief but remains ~13% below February and 20% year-over-year—analysts view it as unreliable relative to actual spending data. Year-ahead inflation expectations fell to 4.6% from 4.8%.
